newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends sharply higher, helped by strike.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends sharply higher, helped by strike.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed sharply higher on Thursday, inspired by the French oil workers' strike and persistent strength of NYMEX products, brokers said.
Dec gas oil closed $5.50 a tonne higher at $229.50, just 75 cents off the session high.
"The U.S. markets have been rallying like mad since the start of the week, and now we're seeing some aggressive short covering in Europe," said one broker.
Dealers said that the breaching of key resistance at $226.50 this morning was significant in firing the rally.
The Dec/Jan backwardation ended 50 cents wider at $2.25 a tonne.
Brokers said that the French oil workers' strike, now in its eighth day, lent support to the rally by hitting volumes on European physical markets.
"But it's not enough justification to the entire move," a broker said. "The spark is really a delayed reaction to U.S. market...that started with a big gasoline move in Monday."
IPE Brent was trading 33 cents higher at $24.11 a barrel at 1755 GMT, around the middle of the day's trading range.
"I think people felt a bit dizzy at the highs but it's fundamentally strong," a dealer said.
The Elf strike is expected to spread to a Shell refinery on December 9 and could escalate into a one-day industry-wide strike in France on December 10, union officials said.
